verdict.rationale: An agent could update block and trust lists programmatically through the Referrals API, and Adyen ships an official MCP server for LLM clients, though the evidence does not show that the MCP server exposes risk tools. Risk profiles and custom rules appear to be managed in the Customer Area, and risk posture is only visible per transaction via webhooks or payment responses. Missing for 10: an API or MCP tool to read risk profiles and rule configuration, programmatic creation or editing of rules (e.g. velocity rules), human approval gates for agent-proposed changes (case management covers transaction review, not rule changes), and evidence that the MCP server covers risk management.
